title: The slain Lamb (Revelation 5)
hookLine: the lion of Judah turns out to be a Lamb that was slain

cards: Someone is crying in the throne room. Not a creature. Not an elder.

John. In the right hand of the one on the throne is a scroll, written inside and on the back, sealed with seven seals. A strong angel calls out: "Who is worthy to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof?"

No one in heaven, on earth or under the earth can do it. And John writes, "I wept much, because no man was found worthy to open and to read the book." Then an elder leans over and tells him to stop crying, and look.

teach.h: HE HEARS: THE LION OF JUDA.
teach.b: First, what John hears: "Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book." The lion reaches back to Jacob's blessing, where Judah is called a lion's whelp.
John is told to expect power.

teach.h: HE SEES: A LAMB, AS IT HAD BEEN SLAIN.
teach.b: Second, what he sees: "and, lo, in the midst of the throne and of the four beasts, and in the midst of the elders, stood a Lamb as it had been slain." He hears lion. He sees lamb.
Wounded, and still standing, at the center of yesterday's room. It has seven horns and seven eyes, the seven Spirits of God, but the text names the wound first. Third, the song.

The creatures and elders fall down and sing a new song: "Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain." Not worthy in spite of being slain. Worthy because of it.

Christians read the Lamb as Jesus, crucified and risen, the one John the Baptist pointed to, as you heard back in year two: "Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world." Fourth, why it matters.

Revelation is full of beasts and dragons and armies. But the one at the center, the one who can open what no one else can, isn't the loudest or the fiercest. It's a lamb that was killed and stands anyway.
In this book, that's what the lion looks like.

how: Christians call Jesus the Lamb of God in worship and prayer; in some forms of the communion service the words 'Lamb of God' (the Agnus Dei) are sung or said before the bread and cup are shared.

games.why: "thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou wast slain." the wound is the reason, not the obstacle.

practice: Bring to mind a moment coming up where you'd usually push, an argument, a deadline, a person who tests you, and picture walking into it as a lamb would: steady and open-handed, not weak, with no fight to prove.
Notice the strength that takes, and let your shoulders drop and your jaw loosen. If you pray, ask God for gentleness in it; if not, rehearse it gently in your mind.

wordCard.voice: The slain Lamb. Announced as a lion, seen as a lamb killed and still standing, and found worthy to open the scroll because it was slain.

orig.note: Greek: lamb. the word Revelation uses for the Lamb in chapter 5.

carryVoice: Your line: the lamb is the lion. Wounded, and still standing at the center. Rest well.
